title: Lester as an independent individualist
summary: Young thought little of Hawkins-style tenors and copied nobody; Kansas City players liked what he did.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: And what was Lester's attitude to other tenor players? Because most tenor players didn't play like him.
They all followed Hawkins rather than his sort of alto style.
What did he feel about them?
Oh, he didn't think nothing of them.
So he was very much an individual.
Very much a man on his own.
I mean, did he have all those characteristics of a man on his own?
He didn't try to copy behind no-body. He just played... He used to play a little baritone, too. Played a nice baritone.
When he was around Kansas City, was he getting the same thing that he got with Fletcher's band, with guys telling him, "Hey man, you should sound more like Coleman Hawkins"?
No. They didn't bother with him.
